clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old woman with a history of endometriosis and prior laparoscopic surgeries presented to the emergency department with acute upper abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Physical examination revealed upper abdominal tenderness. CT imaging demonstrated a partial small bowel obstruction with a transition point at the terminal ileum and an adjacent 1 cm soft-tissue nodule. Three days after admission, she underwent diagnostic laparoscopy, which identified a 2 cm ileal lesion located 4.8 cm from the ileocecal valve with scattered adhesions involving the terminal ileum and right colon. A right hemicolectomy was performed. Pathological examination confirmed endometriosis involving the muscularis propria and serosa of the terminal ileum, ascending colon, and appendix, with a 1.8 × 1.5 × 1.1 cm endometrial mass identified as the cause of the obstruction. The pathology was negative for malignancy. Her post-operative diagnosis was reported as small bowel obstruction and endometriosis of the right round ligament.
